 Magnitude 3.3 Earthquake Strikes Southeast of Petrolia
 Wednesday, 21 October 2026, 7:35 pm Kym Kemp 
 8 comments 
 Screenshot of USGS map 
 A magnitude 3.3 earthquake struck about nine miles southeast of Petrolia at 6:43 p.m. Wednesday, October 21, according to the U.S. Geological Survey .
 The quake occurred at a depth of approximately 6.8 miles.
 The agency’s “Did You Feel It?” listing indicated an intensity of III, corresponding to weak shaking. Residents who felt the earthquake can share their observations with USGS .
 Earthquake magnitudes and other details may be revised as scientists review the data.

 I once asked USGS what the naming policy is, since they kept calling for 18 miles west of Bayside and Bucksport instead of Eureka. At that time the word salad was “using the closest and cutest town name even if no one out of area knows where it is” They don’t do that anymore, now it seems they pick the larger names on the map. But they still cross up Ferndale and Rio Dell all the time and other very odd choices, as here.
